The Mid-Autumn Festival is a traditional East Asian holiday celebrated on the 15th day of the 8th month of the lunar calendar. The full moon is an important symbol of the festival because its round, complete shape represents wholeness, reunion, and togetherness. Mooncakes are traditionally shared with family and friends as a symbol of reunion and togetherness, making them a special part of the celebration. Students who celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival are invited to join us for a mooncake-making gathering on Friday, September 25th at 3:30 PM in the South Church Kitchen. Questions? Please see Ms. Davis in Streeter 255.

Our conversations will be rooted in the Christian faith, but you don’t have to be a Christian or an athlete to come. We’ll meet Friday mornings from 7:00–7:40 on Court 3 in the Field House. FCA is student-led, and we’re looking for students who want to help lead and shape this group. Come check it out this Friday!

For Girls Cross Country, Willa Mantius set the tone for the Academy by securing a top 15 overall finish. The defining highlight of the team’s performance came from its middle pack, where Bailey Qualter and Elsie Kidder ran stride-for-stride through the chute, to seal two crucial scoring positions. The JV team’s charge was ignited by Bella Annello and Wenonah Brewer-Nyborg, who ran virtually shoulder-to-shoulder through the tape. Bella earned 16th place overall, while Wenonah chased her in just three seconds later for 17th overall. Sophomore Lyda Bentley delivered another season-best clocking to keep the Hilltoppers within striking distance, placing 23rd overall.

Of the roughly 700 people on our meal plan, 150 to 200 people come to lunch each day without their ID cards. That’s a lot of people, and it makes the job of our Food Services team more difficult. Please be sure to bring your ID card to lunch and have it ready when you get to the front of the line. Think of it as a small way to say thank you to the people who arrive hours before most of us and work all day to feed us. Having your ID ready is one easy way we can take care of them.

Can you spot the troll? Do you know what a troll is? Members of Mr. Eckhardt’s Contemporary Issues class have been studying Media Literacy, including misinformation and disinformation. If you frequent Ranger Breezeway, you may have seen the opening exhibit of the tiny art gallery that opened on campus last week. Tiny Art Gallery will strike again in October with two shows, the first in celebration of Indigenous People’s Day and the second in celebration of all things spooky. This is a call to all visual artists interested in our tiny project: create a tiny portrait, painting, watercolor, collage within one of these themes. A drop-box with instructions will launch Monday in Student Life. Submissions for the first theme are due Thursday, October 8. Submissions for the spooky theme are due Monday, October 19. You may also submit any questions to Tiny Art Gallery’s anonymous directors via this drop-box.

It’s a Kind of Magic, Sympathy for the Devil, Abracadabra… These are just some of the musical hits inspired by the supernatural in our current age. But did you know there is a long and dark tradition of paranormal-inspired music that predates Queen, The Rolling Stones and Lady Gaga? To hear some of these other voices from the past, you will need to come on the Vermont Symphony Orchestra Halloween concert trip in Burlington on Saturday 10/31. Tickets cost just $15, and you will need to pick up a signed permission slip from the Learning Center, Ranger 110, the Library circulation desk, or Student Life. See Mr. Mackenzie if you have any questions. As Benson Boone reminds us: some opportunities are just too “magical, mystical” to be missed!!

As the weather gets colder, we want to make sure everyone in our community has a warm coat for the season. Free coats are available for students who need or want one. There are a variety of sizes available, so please stop by the Colby lobby and see what is available on the rack labeled ‘free coats’. If you don’t see your size? No problem! Email sjacampuslife@stjacademy.org, and we’ll do our best to help. Staying warm is important, and we’re happy to help however we can!

Our theme of this school year is courage. You all have heard a variety of chapel talks so far this year about ways of being brave in the face of uncertainty. After hearing these stories, it’s normal to ask yourself if you have that kind of courage in you. Sometimes, stories of courage feel like hypotheticals. But we know that these stories of courage belong to you. Recently, the senior class trip chaperones witnessed true courage in our community. On October 4th, many of our seniors visited Six Flags New England for their class trip, a wonderful day filled with special memories. But on the way back on the bus, a student had a serious medical emergency. It was a scary situation, but in moments like these, we are all asked to step up. Thanks in part to the courage shown by some of the students on that bus, everything turned out okay. Every student on that bus did a fantastic job of staying calm, expressing concern, and helping in any way they could…And there is one student in particular who showed us exactly what courage looks like: senior Amuné Greyling. Amuné is part of our Licensed Nurse Assistant training program. She stepped up in a stressful situation, volunteering herself and her expertise to help her classmate in need. She kept calm in a moment where staying calm felt impossible. Her compassion, bravery, and composure were truly remarkable, and we know it will serve her well in her future. We are so proud of you, Amuné! Please join me in celebrating and thanking Amuné.

If you or someone you know is between the ages of 18 and 35, you could have the opportunity to save someone’s life at no cost! This Saturday, at our homecoming football game at LI, Class of 2028 member Andrew Dobbin will be hosting a Bone Marrow and Stem Cell Registry Drive in partnership with Gift of Life Marrow Registry. Every year, tens of thousands of people are diagnosed with blood cancer or other life-threatening diseases and need bone marrow or stem cell transplants to survive. At the game, those between the ages of 18 and 35, and who are in general good health, will be able to do a free, quick cheek swab to join the international bone marrow registry and become a potential match for a patient in need, giving them a second chance at life. Stop by the Gift of Life table at the game to learn more and find out how you can join the registry! It only takes a few minutes to get started, and one small act could make an extraordinary difference. We hope to see you there!
